extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: A shared-task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German. It includes training, development, test, and unannotated data for evaluating NER systems.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled from existing corpora: English data from the Reuters Corpus and German data from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. Training, development, and test sets were selected from specific time periods, and named entity tagging for these sets was done by hand at the University of Antwerp after linguistic preprocessing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters news stories for English and German newspaper articles from the Frankfurter Rundschau extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus; the unannotated data contained 17 million tokens (English) and 14 million tokens (German).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English training/development data were taken from the end of August 1996; English test data were from December 1996; English preprocessed raw data covers September 1996. German training/development/test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992; German raw data were taken from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote names not already in the other categories.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The challenge was to incorporate unannotated data in the learning process; participants used training, development, test, and unannotated data, but no specific augmentation/balancing/sampling procedure is described.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and chunker were applied to the raw data; English data was tagged and chunked by MBT, and German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by Treetagger. Named entity tagging was done by hand.
